title: Bodycam Released in Ohio Freeway Shooter
description:
Submit a tip! Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

Ohio is one of five states that records its traffic cameras. The others being Iowa, Minnesota, Wisconsin, and an East Coast outlier, New Jersey. In a case like freeway shootings or fatal crashes, the cameras have proven invaluable to victims and survivors. Jonathan Myers was transferred to Delaware County Jail. According to court documents, he was charged with 27 felonel felony counts. First degree attempted murder, attempted aggravated murder, second degree felonious assault, discharge of a firearm, on or near a prohibited premise, and having weapons while under disability. Initially, Jonathan pleaded not guilty to all counts, but later changed his plea to not guilty by reason of insanity. A psychological evaluation was conducted and Jonathan was found fit to stand trial. The trial continued and he ultimately entered a plea deal which resulted in convictions for attempted murder, discharge of a firearm on or near a prohibited premise, second-degree felonious assault, and attempted aggravated murder. He was handed down an aggregate 25 to 30-year sentence, which he is currently serving at Trumbull Correctional Institute in northeastern Ohio. His female companion is not suspected of any wrongdoing.
